question: Which valves are directly downstream of pump P-2-1, and which of them has the lowest maximum allowable pressure according to its datasheet?

final.answer: The valves directly downstream of pump P-2-1 are BV-2-1 and PV-2-1. However, neither datasheet states a single maximum allowable pressure: BV-2-1's rating depends on its pressure class, body group and seat material per a pressure/temperature chart, and PV-2-1's rating depends on its body construction and applicable ASME pressure class. Since the datasheets do not specify which pressure class/material each valve actually has, it cannot be determined from the documents which of the two has the lowest maximum allowable pressure (that part is not stated).

cypher:
MATCH (v:PlantItem {tag: 'P-2-1'})-[:line_to]->(d:Valve)
RETURN DISTINCT d.tag AS tag ORDER BY tag

MATCH (d) WHERE d.document_id = 'flowserve-worcester-f51-f52'
  AND (toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'pressure'
       OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029522,'')) CONTAINS 'pressure')
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029520]->(c:plm__PCA_100029524)
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029514]->(f)
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029513]->(s)
RETURN d.plm__PCA_100029521 AS label, d.plm__PCA_100029522 AS value,
       d.lis__datumValue AS number, c.rdfs__label AS caseLabel,
       f.plm__PCA_100029522 AS footnote, s.plm__PCA_100029521 AS sourceTitle,
       d.schema__pageStart AS page
ORDER BY page LIMIT 200

MATCH (d)
WHERE d.document_id = 'fisher-et-d100022x012'
  AND (d:plm__PCA_100029511 OR d:plm__PCA_100029508 OR d:plm__PCA_100029510 OR d:plm__PCA_100029505)
  AND (toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029521,'')) CONTAINS 'pressure'
       OR toLower(coalesce(d.plm__PCA_100029522,'')) CONTAINS 'pressure')
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029520]->(c:plm__PCA_100029524)
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029514]->(f)
OPTIONAL MATCH (d)-[:plm__PCA_100029525]->(s:plm__PCA_100029513)
RETURN d.plm__PCA_100029521 AS label, d.plm__PCA_100029522 AS value,
       c.rdfs__label AS caseLabel, f.plm__PCA_100029522 AS footnote,
       s.plm__PCA_100029521 AS sourceTitle, d.schema__pageStart AS page
LIMIT 200

Datasheet flowserve-worcester-f51-f52, pages [6, 10, 7, 11, 9, 3]:
The maximum allowable pressure depends on the operating temperature and on which pressure class and material (body group or seat material) your valve has — there is no single number. It is given by the pressure/temperature rating chart on page 6, which shows the allowable pressure in bar over temperature in °C for each combination.

Some values from that chart [p. 6] (pressure in bar at the given temperature):

- Group 1.2 Class 150 (Group 1.2 = dual-certified LCB/LCC and WCB/WCC body materials): 19.8 bar at −30 °C, 19.4 bar at 50 °C, 15.8 bar at 150 °C, 12.0 bar at 250 °C
- Group 1.2 Class 300: 51.8 bar at −30 °C / 0 °C, 50.2 bar at 150 °C, 46.4 bar at 250 °C, 42.9 bar at 300 °C
- Group 2.2 Class 150 (Group 2.2 = CF8M body material): 18.9 bar at −30 °C to 38 °C, 13.7 bar at 200 °C
- Group 2.2 Class 300: 49.7 bar at −30 °C, 35.7 bar at 200 °C, 31.6 bar at 300 °C
- Seat materials (examples): Virgin PTFE 47.0 bar at 100 °C, dropping to 0 bar at 228.4 °C; PEEK 47.3 bar at 228.8 °C and 32.8 bar at 250 °C; UHMWPE 51.6 bar at 83.1 °C, 0 bar at 90.6 °C; Delrin 51.7 bar at 79.5 °C; Reinforced PTFE 50.6 bar at 136.9 °C, 0 bar at 229.4 °C

Notes from page 6: the material group ratings come from the ASME B16.34 standard, and the maximum seat temperature limits are listed on page 7. For the exact maximum pressure for your valve, read the chart on page 6 at your operating temperature for your body group and class, and also check the curve for your seat material — the lower of the two applies.

Tool result:
Datasheet fisher-et-d100022x012, pages [4, 3, 5, 32, 18, 26, 19, 22]:
# Maximum Allowable Pressure

There is no single number for maximum allowable pressure — it depends on which valve construction (body material and pressure class) you have. The datasheet says:

**Maximum inlet pressure** is "consistent with" the applicable ASME pressure class of the body, depending on the construction [p. 3]:
- Cast iron bodies, flanged: consistent with CL125B or 250B per ASME B16.1
- Steel and stainless steel bodies, flanged: consistent with CL150, 300 and 600 per ASME B16.34
- Steel and stainless steel bodies, screwed or welding: consistent with flanged CL600 per ASME B16.34
- Or: "as listed below, unless limited by maximum pressure drop or material temperature capabilities"

The pressure ratings listed for steel raised-face valve bodies by variant are [p. 5]: PN16, PN25, PN40, PN63 and PN100 (PN is the EN pressure rating class of the body).

Important warnings repeated throughout the datasheet:
- "The pressure or temperature limits in this bulletin and any applicable code limitations should not be exceeded" [p. 3, 4].
- "Do not exceed the maximum pressure and temperature for the pressure rating of the body material used, even though the trim shown may have higher capabilities" [p. 18, 19, 26].
- Inlet pressure and temperature "must always be limited by the applicable ASME pressure/temperature rating" [p. 32].

**Maximum pressure drop** (the difference between inlet and outlet pressure the valve can handle) equals the maximum inlet pressure for the specific construction, except where further limited; see Figure 13 (standard valves), Figure 14 (Cavitrol III cages, liquid temperature vs pressure drop), or Figure 15 (NACE sour service valves) [p. 3]. For example, Trims 4 and 29 and Trim 85 may be used up to 99 bar / 1440 psi with clean dry gas, but only up to 21 bar / 300 psi with other process fluids [p. 18, 26].

For the **packing system** (the stem seal), the maximum pressure limit given is 1500 psig / 104 bar (at up to 316 °C / 600 °F) for the ENVIRO-SEAL Graphite ULF packing [Table 2, p. 5]. ENVIRO-SEAL PTFE and Duplex packings are limited to 232 °C / 450 °F [Table 2, p. 5].

I could not find in these facts a specific psi/bar value tied to each pressure class or body material — the datasheet points to the ASME B16.34/B16.1 ratings for that.
